## ITEM 1 — THE SMOKE, GENERATED BY THE TIRES (the pass's headline)

Chris's verdict on FP57 Item C: **no smoke visible at all from the cockpit.** His design correction, in his words: "need to get the tires involved in generating the smoke" — and his reference photo (`research/tire-smoke-reference-front.jpg`, READ IT) with his aim: **"but at the front."**

Ground truth (Hal, code read): the TireSmoke emitters are built `local_coords = false` (main.gd ~5835 — world-space particles, a setting inherited from the dust channel, whose birth comment says "so the dust stays") with drift dir (0, 0.75, 0.65) at 1.1–2.4 m/s and NO inherited velocity. At driving speed the car vacates the emission point instantly; the cloud exists only in space the car has left. FP57's proofs all staged standstill or first-contact cases — the one regime where this doesn't apply.

The rework:

- **Generation is per-tire, from the tire's own state.** Each wheel's smoke amount derives from that tire's load × its slip/spin/scrub state — the suspension's per-corner load and the telegraph's per-wheel states are the inputs (a planted tire at its limit generates the cloud; an unloaded or hooked tire generates little or none). The FP57 drive terms (slip at all four, spin at the rears) remain the floor of the model, not the whole of it: load-gating is the new term Chris's sentence adds. If per-corner load is not cleanly available at the emitter update, say so and use the closest honest per-wheel proxy — disclosed, never faked.
- **Emission is born moving.** Particles inherit the car's velocity plus the patch's own throw (the tire's tangential direction at the contact patch), so the cloud boils off the patch and TRAVELS WITH THE CAR for its first life, expanding as it goes — the photo's behaviour: a dense, opaque-white, turbulent cloud that grows as it leaves the tire and engulfs forward around the car. From the seat, a slide at speed must put visible smoke mass in the driver's forward airspace — around the fenders, at the edges of the road view — WHILE the slide happens, not in a trail behind. Front tires in yaw throw theirs across the view.
- **Density is the photo's, not FP57's.** Volume up to the reference's register: this is a cloud, not a wisp. Watch the centre-view discipline from FP56: density at the periphery and low-forward, never a wall across the road ahead. Particle budget stated in the report; the soft billboard construction (FP57) may stay if it carries the density — if it can't, the construction question reopens inside this item and the report says what replaced it.
- **PROOF STANDARD — CHANGED, STANDING FOR THIS CHANNEL:** staged standstill/first-contact captures are BANNED as cockpit-visibility evidence (they have lied twice: FP56, FP57). The proof is a DRIVEN slide at speed (staged DRIVER, real input path, working speed) with DENSE seat frames across the event (10+ fps), showing the cloud present in the forward airspace during the slide, plus the sync witness (smoke amount vs per-tire state) on the same run. If the driven proof rig cannot produce a real slide at speed, the report says so plainly and the item ships as UNPROVEN rather than staged-proven.

## ITEM 2 — FLAME RE-AIM (one constant)

Chris: "the flame jets are cool, but think theyre point wrong way... back at angle feel more right, or straight up." As built: holders at (±0.50, 0.74, −1.98), aim `dir57 = (±0.82, 0.18, −0.54)` — out/up/FORWARD (Godot −Z is car-forward; +Z is rearward). Re-aim to **backward at an angle**: the horizontal component flips rearward (out/back/up in the same proportions is the starting candidate: (±0.82, 0.18, +0.54)); probe-verify the holder basis reads the new direction exactly (the FP57 orthonormalization check re-run). If the builder's own staged-shift frames suggest the angle reads wrong from the seat position, straight up (0, 1, ±small out) is the pre-approved alternative — pick ONE, state which and why; do not ship both switchable. Everything else about the channel (envelope, boost flame, alive gating, stage-74 terms) untouched.

## ITEM 3 — TERRAIN: THE LOW EDGE RULES

Chris: "one shallow part seems to sink into sand on a corner." Hal's mechanism (code read, conviction is the builder's job): `_world57_terrain_y(fr, lat)` builds the apron from the frame's CENTRE (`pos.y + rel`, rel −0.62 at lat 0) and measures meet against the centreline field — but the frame carries `up`, and a banked section's low edge sits at centre − hw·(up's lateral tilt): at hw 6 and 25° of bank, ~2.5 m below centre. FP57's stage-75 under-road check measured at centre only — the one place the defect cannot occur.

The fix: the terrain height under the road derives from the road section's LOW EDGE, not its centre: for each station, compute both edge heights from the frame (`pos ± side·hw`, projected on `up`), take the lower, and key the apron's meet profile to that — ground shoulders under the lowest point of the section with the same −0.62 register, everywhere, banked or not. The valley blend and the gap rule (no earth rises to a gap) are preserved; where keying to the low edge would pile earth against a high edge on a steep bank, the apron follows the low edge and falls away from the high side — state the rule chosen in the report if a conflict case exists.

Proof: stage 75 gains an EDGE census — per track, the minimum terrain clearance under EITHER road edge across all stations, stated as a number (target: the −0.62 register holds within measurement tolerance at the edges, no station where terrain meets or exceeds an edge); plus a seat capture at a banked shallow corner (builder finds the worst-census station and shoots there — the census names the corner, the capture proves the read).
